Maya (CS): Heads-up: BeaconHealth flagged a surprise spike — embeddings usage up 3.6x in 48h after they onboarded the clinical-ontology feed. Renewal QBR in 12 days. We should prepare a cost-first primer and an ops checklist.
Ravi (AE): Is this a one-off import or continuous stream?
Maya (CS): Looks like a nightly bulk job plus lots of small inference calls from their UI. The bulk job is the main culprit.
Noemi (Solutions Eng): Quick wins: 1) Switch bulk-import to batched embedding calls (batch_size=512) and async job with retry/backoff. 2) Introduce a dedupe pass to avoid duplicate vectors. 3) Add per-job sampling during initial ingest.
Noemi (Solutions Eng): Example batching config for Redwood Console (apply to route /v1/embeddings):
```json
{
  "route": "/v1/embeddings",
  "batching": {
    "mode": "fixed",
    "max_items": 512,
    "timeout_ms": 250
  },
  "async_ingest": true,
  "dedupe": {
    "enabled": true,
    "strategy": "hash_prefix"
  }
}
```
CostBot: alert: account_usage.beaconhealth > expected_monthly_embeddings * 3.0 (triggered at 2835001003).
Liam (Finance): If this trajectory continues, they blow past the next tier and it materially changes renewal pricing. I need a projected spend table for the QBR.
Ravi (AE): Customer wants non-disruptive fixes first. No hard rate limits without SRE sign-off. Can we present an opt-in 'ingest throttle' option?
Noemi (Solutions Eng): Yes — propose an opt-in throttled ingest window (02:00-06:00 local) + a commit to do batch-size tuning.
Maya (CS): I'll run enablement session with their data team tomorrow 11am ET to walk the batching and dedupe plan. Will capture feedback and any blocker notes.
ProductPulseBot: feedback: BeaconHealth requested a per-batch cost estimate in the Console UX. Logged as product_request-6421.
Liam (Finance): For the QBR, use three scenarios: (A) no changes (B) batching + dedupe (C) batching + dedupe + quantized embed model. Use current month baseline + projected nightly import rates. I'll drop the table into the one-pager.
Ravi (AE): I'll draft the one-pager: problem statement, remediation steps taken, 3-scenario spend table, recommended commit ask.
Noemi (Solutions Eng): Follow-up audit: I'll run a quick sampling of their top 500 vectors to estimate dedupe yield and share expected percent reduction.
Maya (CS): Also capturing onboarding status: they finished platform onboarding but haven't yet consumed the 'cost-awareness' enablement. Add that to the enablement checklist for tomorrow.
Ravi (AE): Can we offer a small onboarding credit if they agree to a 12-month commit? That might ease negotiation.
Liam (Finance): I can model the credit. Show me projected delta between tiers and impact of a $X credit (we'll compute $ later).
Maya (CS): Action list: Maya - run enablement & capture notes; Noemi - dedupe audit + batch config PR; Ravi - one-pager + renewal ask; Liam - spend scenarios and credit modeling.
Maya (CS): I'll also collect direct customer feedback in the call and ping ProductPulseBot with the verbatim ask for per-batch cost estimates.
ProductPulseBot: note: survey sent to BeaconHealth SREs post-call (id: pb-2835).
Noemi (Solutions Eng): Small technical note: enabling dedupe can be CPU-heavy during initial pass; recommend staging window and a rolling dedupe to avoid SRE pain.
Maya (CS): Good call. We'll include staging plan in the runbook.
Ravi (AE): Scheduling: QBR prep review in 3 days. I'll send invites and attach the draft one-pager.
Liam (Finance): I'll upload the spend tables in that doc before the meeting.
Maya (CS): Thanks team :white_check_mark: I'll post the runbook and friction notes here after the enablement session.
CostBot: info: ticket CS-8612 created for BeaconHealth ingest optimization.
